clue.text: Shoo flies away regularly in dungeon

indicators.note: every other letter goes away at a steady interval, leaving a regular sequence behind

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters are kept

explanation.surface: Someone shooing insects out of a dank underground cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole is slang for a grim prison cell, the kind of place a dungeon is.

clue.text: December over, Mr Simpson set about furnishing for the house

indicators.note: something set about another surrounds it

parts.note: Homer Simpson of The Simpsons
calendar abbreviation
o is short for over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: After Christmas, Homer Simpson gets busy redecorating.
explanation.definitionFit: Home decor is interior furnishing and decoration of a dwelling.

clue.text: Bedding Soviet hero with stomach upset

indicators.note: the stomach is the middle of a word, and upset in a down clue means turned upside down

parts.note: Lenin, founder of the Soviet state

explanation.surface: A revered Soviet leader in his sickbed with tummy trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the middle three letters are turned round, leaving the outer letters in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is a collective word for sheets and pillowcases, bed linen.

clue.text: Image made by copper, spun titanium and iron

indicators.note: something spun round faces the other way, so the symbols are read backwards

parts.note: chemical symbol for titanium
chemical symbol for iron, from Latin ferrum

explanation.surface: Police artwork made, oddly, from spun metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a third element (Cu) but belongs to the definition: a copper is a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-FIT is a computer-generated likeness of a suspect, compiled by police from witness descriptions.

clue.text: Awfully bashful Pound papped with the help of this?

definitions.text: papped with the help of this?

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters come out in a mess

parts.note: taken as written
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: Shy poet Ezra Pound snapped by paparazzi.
explanation.walkthrough: Pound looks like the poet Ezra Pound, but is the unit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashbulb gives the burst of light paparazzi use when photographing celebrities.

clue.text: Carries off totally, as they say nowadays

definitions.meaning: second meaning: modern slang clipping of totally

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition flags modern youth slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry, and totes is current slang for totally, as in totes amazing.

clue.text: Spare tyre short of a blow

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so that item is taken out

parts.note: a spare tyre is a roll of fat round the belly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A motorist lacking a spare wheel has suffered a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare tyre' is British slang for a paunch, a fat stomach; remove its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A punch is a blow struck with the fist.

clue.text: Deep in a forest, carrying protective clothing

indicators.note: the words carry the answer, holding it within them

parts.note: runs across the words, starting at the end of the first

explanation.surface: Someone lost deep in the woods, holding on to their coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is an apron or sleeveless garment worn to keep clothes clean.

clue.text: Reasonable to boot Nad out?

indicators.note: letters put out of place lose their original order

parts.note: the raw letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Asking whether kicking out someone called Nad is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Not too bad means acceptable or fair enough, a synonym of reasonable.

clue.text: Free marketeer getting yes vote in Hong Kong

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: standard abbreviation
aye is a yes vote in Parliament

explanation.surface: A capitalist economist wins approval in Hong Kong's open economy.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Hayek was the Austrian economist famed for championing free markets.

clue.text: Cherries perhaps scared to take on United

indicators.note: taking something on means taking it inside

parts.note: frit is British dialect for frightened
standard abbreviation, as in football club names

explanation.surface: The Cherries, a football team, are afraid of playing a United side.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cherries is AFC Bournemouth's nickname, which steers toward football.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherries are an example of fruit, signalled by perhaps.

clue.text: Cameo suitable for child actor?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small role in a play or film
second meaning, punning: a role for a minor, someone under age

explanation.walkthrough: Minor is read twice: small in importance, and a person under the legal age.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a brief appearance, the very definition of a small role; a child is legally a minor.

clue.text: Mad Dog losing his head, in a state?

indicators.note: placed in something means set inside it

parts.note: abbreviation for New York state

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is lost here

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A rabid dog, beheaded, in a sorry condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutty is informal for crazy, a synonym of mad.

clue.text: Scholarly boozer back in the money!

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: dosh is British slang for money

indicators.note: going back means running in the opposite direction

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub

explanation.surface: An academic drinker celebrates being flush again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back in the money' reads as one phrase meaning rich again, but splits into a turnaround and an insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Donnish describes the manner of a university don: bookish, learned, academic.

clue.text: Have the hump when touring rotten, backward county

indicators.note: touring something means going round it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to have the hump is British slang for being in a sulk

indicators.note: backward means read from the end towards the start

parts.note: food gone off is rotten

explanation.surface: Someone sulks while touring a decaying rural backwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward county' looks like an insult to a rural place, but backward applies only to the word for rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffolk is one of the counties of eastern England.

clue.text: Joker or Jack?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an amusing, eccentric person, a joker
second meaning: the jack is a playing ...

explanation.walkthrough: Joker and Jack both look like playing cards; the joker is in fact read as a comic person.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is a wag or comedian; the jack is an example of a playing card, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Back in the saddle, doctor put in moulded denture

indicators.note: put in means placed inside
something moulded is reshaped into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
medical officer

explanation.surface: A dentist back at work fitting false teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like the anagram signal; here it is the inserted MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Remounted means having got back on a horse, literally back in the saddle.

clue.text: Mug delivering relief?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gullible person, easily fooled
second meaning: a boiled sweet or lolly sucked to soothe a sore throat

explanation.walkthrough: Mug wants to be a cup; it is the British word for a dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: A sucker is someone easily conned, like a mug; a sucker is also a lolly that soothes when sucked.

clue.text: He rocked the kimono, amazingly

indicators.note: something amazing defies expectation, so the letters end up in an unexpected order

parts.note: the raw letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone looked stunning in a kimono.
explanation.walkthrough: Keith Moon was the wild drummer of The Who.
explanation.definitionFit: Keith Moon was a rock drummer, so he rocked.

clue.text: Airline — the ultimate in losing luggage!

parts.note: British Airways

indicators.note: the ultimate part of a word is its final letter

parts.note: final letter of losing

explanation.surface: A complaint about an airline that is the best at mislaying cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag is a piece of luggage, a case or holdall.

clue.text: Jealous chap announced takeover stake in company stock

parts.note: green with envy

indicators.note: announced means said out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a chap is a male

explanation.surface: An envious man reveals he is buying into a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenmail is buying a big stake in a firm and threatening takeover so the company buys the shares back at a premium.

clue.text: Very miserable wife gagged

parts.note: standard abbreviation
to gag is to retch

explanation.surface: A spouse is deeply unhappy and was silenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gagged' suggests being silenced, but here it is the sense of nearly vomiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Wretched means in a state of deep distress or unhappiness.

clue.text: The odd drink?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: old British slang for strange
second meaning: a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like the occasional tipple; the adjective is in fact a synonym of strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is a British informal word for peculiar, and also the spirit made from sugar cane.

clue.text: Religious leader beginning to talk the talk!

parts.note: a rabbi leads a Jewish congregation

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the first talk

explanation.surface: A preacher about to start delivering the right words.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbit is British slang for chatter, as in 'all that rabbit', from rhyming slang rabbit and pork, talk. The word talk appears twice: the first gives its initial, the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbit is British slang for idle chatter, so it can stand for the talk.

clue.text: Cash book's limitless margin

indicators.note: without limits means without its two boundary letters

parts.note: a ledger is an accounts book

explanation.surface: An accounts book with an unlimited profit margin.
explanation.walkthrough: Margin looks like a business term chiming with cash book; it is the border sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is the border of something, synonymous with a margin.

clue.text: Medic, attractive bloke, leaving hospital lit

parts.note: abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: the abbreviation leaving the word means it is removed

parts.note: a hunk is a handsome man
standard abbreviation, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A doctor and a handsome man stepping out of a brightly lit hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lit' at the end reads as illuminated; it is slang for intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit is slang for intoxicated, a synonym of drunk.

clue.text: Token opposition action?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a disc used in board games
second meaning: a move made in response to oppose another

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a merely token protest by a political opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A counter is a small game piece; a counter is also a retaliatory response, as in a counterattack.

clue.text: Banter with husband in greasy spoon

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: a greasy spoon is a cheap British café, informally a caff
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Joking with one's spouse over a fry-up in a café.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaff is to tease good-humouredly, a synonym of banter.

clue.text: Hold off with fencing sword mostly grasped with both hands

indicators.note: something grasped is held inside the hands

parts.note: right and left, abbreviated

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: the épée is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: A fencer fends off an attack, gripping the weapon two-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel is to drive back or ward off an attacker.

clue.text: Strong Asian currency achieved by effort

parts.note: hard as in tough
the won is the currency of Korea

explanation.surface: A robust Asian currency earned by hard graft.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-won describes something gained only through great struggle and labour.

clue.text: Mad King visiting US siege city

indicators.note: visiting a place means going inside it

parts.note: Waco, Texas, scene of the 1993 Branch Davidian siege
chess abbreviation

explanation.surface: An insane monarch drops in on a besieged American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Wacko is slang for crazy, a synonym of mad.

clue.text: Answer long letter

parts.note: standard abbreviation for answer
to itch for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Reply to a lengthy piece of correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the spelt-out name of the letter H.

clue.text: Arizona city spies vote to leave the old country

indicators.note: what leaves departs from the word, so it is dropped

parts.note: Phoenix is the capital of Arizona
a cross marks a vote on a ballot
the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: American agents abroad cast votes before quitting their homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: The spies are placed after the city once its X is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoenicia was an ancient seafaring civilisation on the coast of modern Lebanon.

clue.text: Dull American Democrat arrested by G-man

indicators.note: someone arrested is held within custody, so these go inside

parts.note: a G-man or fed is an FBI agent
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A boring US politician taken in by the FBI.
explanation.definitionFit: Faded colours have lost brightness, so they are dull.

clue.text: "Misspeak" about new policy

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: misspeak is a politician's euphemism for telling a lie, hence the quotes
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A politician fudges talk of a fresh policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A line is a stance or official position, as in the party line.

clue.text: British Member of Parliament for York?

definitions.note: verb: to york a batsman is to bowl him with a yorker

parts.note: standard abbreviation
a group of owls is called a parliament

explanation.surface: Asking who sits as the MP for York.
explanation.walkthrough: MP looks political, but a member of a parliament of owls is an owl. In cricket, a yorker is a ball pitched at the batsman's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To york a batsman is to dismiss him with a yorker, a kind of delivery bowled in cricket.
